name: truSculpt iD

lead: truSculpt iD is a non-invasive radiofrequency device used to slim localized fat on areas such as the abdomen. It sits alongside freezing, laser and ultrasound approaches to non-surgical fat reduction.

Radiofrequency energy heats fat tissue while the skin is kept cooler, with the aim of reducing fat thickness over time. Many small registered trials of truSculpt devices exist (4 to 70 participants), along with published studies of related monopolar RF devices, including a 2020 ultrasound study on the abdomen and flanks.

paras: It is a clinic treatment with a handheld applicator over the target area, usually described as needing no incisions or downtime.
No device-specific safety data were retrieved.

angle.text: People consider it for non-invasive slimming of localized fat: RF heating of the fat layer reduces fat over time and leaves a slimmer treated area. Many small trials are registered, with few published results for this specific device.

lead: truSculpt iD is a non-invasive radiofrequency (RF) body-contouring device from Cutera for localized fat reduction, with related truSculpt devices registered in trials since 2009.[1][2] Radiofrequency is one of several energy modalities used for non-invasive fat reduction, alongside cryotherapy, ultrasound and laser.[3]

Published evidence includes a 2020 ultrasound study of a temperature-controlled multi-frequency monopolar RF device on the abdomen and flanks,[3] a 2017 study of 1-MHz monopolar RF for lower facial fat,[4] and a series of registered truSculpt trials of 4 to 70 participants.[1][2][5]

paras: The abstract of a 2020 study describes high-frequency monopolar RF as raising fat temperature enough to reduce its thickness without excessively heating the skin.[3] A 2024 review in Clinics in Plastic Surgery mentions truSculpt flex, an electrical muscle stimulation device, among non-invasive tools one surgeon uses with surgery.[6]

A 2020 study in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology used ultrasound to evaluate a single treatment with a temperature-controlled monopolar RF device for localized abdominal and flank adiposity; the authors noted that two devices had previously been shown to reduce fat thickness on ultrasound after one treatment.[3] A 2017 study of static monopolar 1-MHz RF assessed facial fat reduction and tightening of the lower face.[4] Full results were not available for this article.

Registered trials sponsored for the truSculpt device include a pivotal circumferential reduction study of 70 people for abdominal fat starting in 2016,[2] a 44-person thigh circumference study from 2012,[5] and smaller studies on lipolysis, wrinkles, cellulite and tissue tightening between 2017 and 2018.[7][8][9] Most records list the studies as completed, but no outcome data were retrieved.
No safety data specific to truSculpt iD were retrieved for this article.

timeline.event: A truSculpt thigh circumference reduction study is registered (terminated).[1]
Pivotal circumferential reduction study for abdominal fat begins.[2]
Several truSculpt pilot, follow-up and wrinkle studies begin.[7][8]
